clue.text: accepted by mother

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'accepted by mother (7)': its opening words are missing, so neither the definition nor the piece that MUM takes in can be identified; no scan, and a search found nothing.

clue.text: Doctor's sobriety reduced by half-half!

parts.note: MO, a medical officer, is a common abbreviation for a doctor

indicators.note: only half of the word sobriety is kept, here its second four letters

explanation.surface: A tipsy exclamation that the doctor's sobriety is only half what it was.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's last 'half' is the definition; the earlier 'reduced by half' is the instruction to keep the back half of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A moiety is a formal or legal word for one of two equal portions of something.

clue.text: Remove pests from most of valley and river

indicators.note: the last letter of the synonym is dropped, leaving most of it

parts.note: a dell is a small wooded valley
the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: Pest control in a riverside valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims DELL to DEL; the OUSE is the name of several English rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: To delouse is to rid a person or animal of lice, which are pests.

clue.text: Agents limiting working to arrange groups of companies

indicators.note: the agency's letters close in on either side, limiting what sits between them

parts.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency, so its agents
on means working, as a machine that is on
to sort is to arrange

explanation.surface: Spies hemming in work to set up business groups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agents' looks like a plural noun for people, but stands for the agency whose initials go round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Consortia, plural of consortium, are associations of businesses joined for a shared venture.

clue.text: Film star eliminated crooks, embracing love

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the next piece inside them, as arms hold someone
to crook is to bend, so the word eliminated is bent out of shape and its letters rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, so O

explanation.surface: A screen hero wiped out the criminals while hugging a sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooks' rearranges ELIMINATED as MATINEEIDL, and 'embracing' puts O for love between its D and L.
explanation.definitionFit: A matinee idol is a handsome actor adored by audiences, a movie heart-throb.

clue.text: Potential flower came up with a partner

parts.note: rose is the past tense of rise, so came up
bud, short for buddy, is a pal or partner

explanation.surface: Someone appeared along with a companion.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosebud is an unopened rose, a bloom that has not yet flowered.

clue.text: Score gets one out of defeat

indicators.note: one is taken out of the word for defeat

parts.note: ruin means defeat or downfall
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A team's score loses a player when defeat looms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes I (one) from RUIN. A run is the scoring unit in cricket and baseball.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket and baseball a run is a single point scored.

clue.text: Get rid of poor quality land

definitions.meaning: to ... a plan is to cancel or drop it
land covered with stunted bushes and little else

explanation.definitionFit: To scrub is informally to cancel, and the noun also names rough ground covered in stunted vegetation.

clue.text: British charm includes very good style

indicators.note: the word for charm takes the next piece inside it

parts.note: an aura is a distinctive, attractive atmosphere about someone

explanation.surface: British appeal contains something very fine and stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravura is great technical skill and brilliance shown in a performance.

clue.text: Some Europeans tend much to vary

indicators.note: the letters of the words before are told to vary, changing their arrangement

explanation.surface: A remark that certain Europeans tend to vary a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to vary' rearranges TEND and MUCH into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dutchmen are men from the Netherlands, a European country.

clue.text: I put out fashionable folk in London area

parts.note: to sling is to throw, put out or chuck
the ton is an old word for fashionable society

explanation.surface: Someone ejected trendy people from a smart part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Islington is a borough of north London, known for its fashionable residents.
explanation.definitionFit: Islington is a district and borough in north London.

clue.text: List without hesitation includes a main course

indicators.note: the shortened list takes the next letter inside it
the hesitation sound is taken away from the list

parts.note: a roster is a list of names on duty
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A menu without dithering has a main dish on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'List' reads as a verb in the surface, but it is the noun for the duty roster.
explanation.definitionFit: A roast, meat cooked in the oven, is a typical main dish of a meal.

clue.text: City, ancient city, surrounded by much of ancient city

indicators.note: the first old city sits inside the second, which goes round it
the final letter is dropped, leaving most of the word

parts.note: Troy is the ancient city of the Trojan War
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city

explanation.surface: A city is ringed by the remains of an ancient one.
explanation.walkthrough: The two 'ancient city' phrases are different cities. Truro is the cathedral city of Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: Truro is a cathedral city, the county town of Cornwall in south-west England.

clue.text: It's used to scrub or fix black fly

parts.note: to nail something is to fix it in place
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
to rush is to fly, go very quickly

explanation.surface: A gadget for cleaning or for pinning a dark insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly' looks like the insect, but it is the verb meaning to hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: A nailbrush is a small stiff brush for cleaning fingernails.

clue.text: Screen in Assisi not, sadly, holding firm?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the next piece inside them
the words Assisi and not are arranged badly, sadly mixed up

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A question whether a screen in Assisi might fail to hold firm.
explanation.walkthrough: Assisi, an Italian church town, is only a decoy for the surface; its letters are the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An iconostasis is the screen covered in icons that separates the sanctuary in an Orthodox church.

clue.text: Limit to consumption's most desirable in front of partner

parts.note: best means most desirable
before can mean in front of, as in standing before a judge
a date is a romantic partner for an evening

explanation.surface: Advice that a good partner is the most desirable thing to set before you.
explanation.walkthrough: A best-before date is printed on food packaging in Britain to show when it should be eaten by.
explanation.definitionFit: The date printed on food after which it should not be eaten sets a deadline for eating it.

clue.text: One avoids any microbe evolving in early stages

indicators.note: the letters change form as they evolve into a new arrangement
the letter for one is left out of the word any

parts.note: a means one, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Something steers clear of any microbe that is still developing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoids' takes A from ANY to leave NY, and 'evolving' rearranges NY plus MICROBE.
explanation.definitionFit: Embryonic describes something at a rudimentary, undeveloped beginning, like an embryo.

clue.text: Bike race starts to spoil country walk

indicators.note: the first letters of the next two words are taken

parts.note: a ramble is a leisurely walk in the countryside

explanation.surface: Motorbikes racing about begin to ruin a hike through the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' gives S and C, the first letters of 'spoil' and 'country'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scramble is a motorcycle race over rough, hilly terrain.

clue.text: Mates down under receiving various pardons from traditional opponents

indicators.note: the word for mates takes the next piece inside it

parts.note: cobbers is Australian slang for mates or friends

indicators.note: the letters of pardons are put in various orders, mixed up

explanation.surface: Australian friends getting assorted pardons from old enemies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mates down under' points to Australian slang; 'from' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Police and criminals are the classic adversaries, and the name of the children's chasing game.

clue.text: Small group interrupting glib nationalist

indicators.note: the group breaks into the middle of the word for glib

parts.note: pat means glib, too ready, as in a pat answer
a trio is a small group of three

explanation.surface: A trio heckles a smooth-talking flag-waver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'glib' is an adjective here, and 'pat' in the sense of a too-ready answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriot is someone who loves and zealously supports their country.

clue.text: Runs I later scrambled in second test

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: the letters are scrambled, stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A cricket report on runs made in a later match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrambled' rearranges R, I and LATER.
explanation.definitionFit: A retrial is a second hearing of a case in court, trying it again.

clue.text: Very fat roofer ignoring one stableman

parts.note: OS, outsize, is the clothing label for very large sizes

indicators.note: the letter for one is left out, ignored

parts.note: a tiler lays tiles on roofs
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A very large roofer, leaving someone out, becomes a stable hand.
explanation.walkthrough: OS (outsize) is a British clothing-size label for very large garments.
explanation.definitionFit: An ostler was the man who looked after horses at an inn.

clue.text: Flier — leading one among a high-class group

indicators.note: these two pieces go in among the others

parts.note: U is the old label for upper-class usage
a lot is a group or set of things
top means leading, as in top of the table
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An aviator heading a single seat in an elite party.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class comes from the 1950s British distinction between U and non-U speech.
explanation.definitionFit: An autopilot is a device that flies an aircraft automatically.

clue.text: Italian city flat -gold must be handed over

parts.note: a pad is informal for a flat or home

indicators.note: the symbol for gold is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Someone in an Italian flat has to surrender gold.
explanation.walkthrough: Padua is the English name of Padova in north-east Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Padua is a city in the Veneto region of northern Italy.

clue.text: It is chasing the old monsters

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so this piece follows

parts.note: ye is an archaic form of the
'tis is a contraction of it is

explanation.surface: A tale of something pursuing the creatures of old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It is' gives the poetic contraction 'tis, and 'chasing' means coming after.
explanation.definitionFit: Yetis are legendary ape-like creatures said to live in the Himalayas.

clue.text: Difficulty bringing in long shade

indicators.note: the word for difficulty brings the next letter inside it

parts.note: a bind is an awkward difficulty

explanation.surface: Trouble arises in fetching a long shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' is the abbreviation L, not a verb meaning to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: A blind is a screen over a window that shuts out light.

clue.text: Lateness I put to rights-that's vital

indicators.note: to put something to rights is to set it in order, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone insists that fixing their lateness is crucial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put to rights' rearranges LATENESS and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Essential means absolutely necessary, indispensable.

clue.text: Have a meal — some have a teacake

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are taken, a run within them

explanation.surface: Advice to dine on a teacake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' points to EAT inside 'have a teacake'. A teacake is a British sweet bun.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat is to consume food, as at a meal.

clue.text: Competitor, even though losing heart, went fast in races

indicators.note: the middle letters of the word even are lost
the past tense of run goes inside the races

parts.note: TT, Tourist Trophy, is the motorcycle races on the Isle of Man
ran means went fast

explanation.surface: A rival, though dispirited, sped through the races.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle races on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrant is someone who enters a contest, a competitor.
